text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a gated sweep comparing fused-attn vs flashvariant on the paged-attn branch after yesterday's allocator swap. seeing ~12% p99 regressions for long sequences (8k+).

alex: can you drop the benchmark config and the exact metric numbers?

maria: test rig: 8xA100, model=redwood-13b-flashv2-quant, seq=8192, batch=1/2, kv-pages=64k, allocator=arena+mixed-slab (the new change). p50 ~ stable, p95 +4%, p99 +12% (token gen).

liam: interesting. p95 small but p99 jump suggests a tail caused by misc IO or evictions. did you see more page faults in the runtime telemetry?

maria: yes — host-level trace shows spike in page-reads per second right when blocktable crosses ~1.1M entries. attached microtrace: ``
[profile snippet]
attn_kernel: fused_fast    48%
attn_kernel: flash_fallback 42%
kv_pager: read_io_wait  78ms avg}

nathan: that fallback % is suspicious. kernel selector might be choosing flash_fallback when contiguous blocks are fragmented by the new allocator. fragmented pages => larger scatter-gather for KV pages => slower kv read => selector avoids fused kernel.

alex: can you paste the allocator histogram? slab sizes vs small allocations?

maria: allocator histogram (top): ``
small_bucket(64): 120k
small_bucket(128): 80k
slab_4k: 12k
arena_frag(>1MB chunk): 45% used
blocktable_nodes: 1.2M
``

liam: so mixed-slab left a lot of <4k fragments in the arena — blocktable nodes are spread and not contiguous. that explains full-KV prefetch misses.

maria: i ran an experiment toggling prefetch_window from 4->8 (heuristic used in paged-attn scheduler). result: p99 drops to +2% and the kernel fallback rate halves.

nathan: good signal. so mitigations: 1) allocator change to favor contiguous extents for blocktable allocations, 2) bump prefetch_window for long seq canaries, 3) tweak kernel selector to prefer flash variant with more aggressive async prefetch.

alex: patch idea: add a 'blocktable_hint' allocator path that requests contiguous slabs (power-of-two pages) for blocktable growth. cheap in headroom. open a draft PR?

maria: opened draft PR #5287 with perf numbers and microtrace. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/paged-attn/pull/5287

dev-bot: Deploy plan created for canary -> canary-2 (10% traffic). CI: 4/4 green.

liam: i'll run the litmus harness (end-to-end with kernel switch telemetry) and post results here. expecting to validate the allocator_hint + prefetch tweak.

maria: quick note — fused-attn still wins on isolated throughput tests. this is mainly about the interaction between KV paging and allocation layout causing kernel-selector thrash.

nathan: also check batching heuristics: current continuous-batching groups by arrival time which can mix different seq-lens causing larger KV working set. try grouping by seq-length bucket for batching. small change, potentially large tail improvement.

alex: good call. try seq-bucket batcher with warmup window 20ms. if stable, roll to canary after allocator patch.

maria: thanks — i'll coordinate the canary today and share the final microbench and tracer. will include flame and kv-pager heatmap.

liam: +1. follow-up: if allocator changes aren't enough, we may add a compact-on-threshold pass for blocktable growth during low load. but that's more invasive.

maria: putting that as plan-C. for now plan-A = allocator hint + prefetch_window bump + seq-bucket batching experiment.

nathan: noted. i'll create an experiment ticket and mark dependent telemetry flags.

maria: thanks all, will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
